1: # Tabs Component
2: 
3: ### Tabs
4: 
5: ```typescript
6: @ComponentV2
7: struct TabsDemo {
8:   @Local currentIndex: number = 0;
9:   @Local tabController: TabsController = new TabsController();
10: 
11:   @Builder
12:   TabBuilder(title: string, targetIndex: number, icon: Resource) {
13:     Column() {
14:       Image(icon)
15:         .width(24)
16:         .height(24)
17:         .opacity(this.currentIndex === targetIndex ? 1 : 0.6)
18:       Text(title)
19:         .fontSize(12)
20:         .fontColor(this.currentIndex === targetIndex ? '#007AFF' : '#8E8E93')
21:         .fontWeight(this.currentIndex === targetIndex ? FontWeight.Medium : FontWeight.Normal)
22:         .margin({ top: 4 })
23:     }
24:     .width('100%')
25:     .height(56)
26:     .justifyContent(FlexAlign.Center)
27:     .onClick(() => {
28:       this.currentIndex = targetIndex;
29:       this.tabController.changeIndex(targetIndex);
30:     })
31:   }
32: 
33:   build() {
34:     Tabs({ barPosition: BarPosition.End, controller: this.tabController }) {
35:       TabContent() {
36:         HomePage()
37:       }
38:       .tabBar(this.TabBuilder('Home', 0, $r('app.media.home')))
39: 
40:       TabContent() {
41:         DiscoverPage()
42:       }
43:       .tabBar(this.TabBuilder('Discover', 1, $r('app.media.discover')))
44: 
45:       TabContent() {
46:         ProfilePage()
47:       }
48:       .tabBar(this.TabBuilder('Profile', 2, $r('app.media.profile')))
49:     }
50:     .barMode(BarMode.Fixed)  // or BarMode.Scrollable
51:     .barHeight(56)
52:     .animationDuration(300)
53:     .onChange((index: number) => {
54:       this.currentIndex = index;
55:     })
56:   }
57: }
58: ```

1: # ArkTS Language Guide
2: 
3: ArkTS is a TypeScript superset optimized for HarmonyOS with strict static typing enforcement and UI declaration extensions.
4: 
5: ## Key Differences from TypeScript
6: 
7: ### Prohibited Features (Critical!)
8: 
9: ArkTS **strictly prohibits** these TypeScript features. Using them will cause **compilation errors**:
10: 
11: ```typescript
12: // ❌ These TypeScript features are NOT allowed in ArkTS
13: 
14: // 1. any type - ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN
15: let data: any;  // Compilation Error!
16: 
17: // 2. unknown type
18: let value: unknown;  // Error!
19: 
20: // 3. Type assertions
21: (value as string).length;  // Error!
22: (<SomeType>data).method();  // Error!
23: 
24: // 4. Dynamic property access (without Record type)
25: let obj = {};
26: obj['key'] = value;  // Error! (unless Record type)
27: 
28: // 5. Structural typing for classes
29: class A { x: number = 0; }
30: class B { x: number = 0; }
31: let a: A = new B();  // Error! Classes must be explicitly related
32: 
33: // 6. typeof for types
34: type T = typeof someVariable;  // Error!
35: 
36: // 7. keyof operator
37: type Keys = keyof SomeType;  // Error!
38: 
39: // 8. Indexed access types
40: type Value = SomeType['key'];  // Error!
41: 
42: // 9. Conditional types
43: type Check<T> = T extends string ? 'yes' : 'no';  // Error!
44: 
45: // 10. Mapped types
46: type Readonly<T> = { readonly [P in keyof T]: T[P] };  // Error!
47: 
48: // 11. Symbol type
49: const sym = Symbol('key');  // Error!
50: 
51: // 12. Decorators on non-class elements (except specific ArkTS decorators)
52: ```
53: 
54: ### Allowed Patterns (ArkTS-Specific)
55: 
56: ```typescript
57: // ✅ These patterns are supported and recommended
58: 
59: // 1. Explicit types
60: let data: string = 'hello';
61: let count: number = 42;
62: let flag: boolean = true;
63: 
64: // 2. Interfaces
65: interface User {
66:   id: string;
67:   name: string;
68:   age?: number;  // Optional properties OK
69: }
70: 
71: // 3. Type aliases (basic)
72: type UserId = string;
73: type Callback = (data: string) => void;
74: type Status = 'loading' | 'success' | 'error';  // Union types
75: 
76: // 4. Record type for dynamic keys
77: let map: Record<string, number> = {};
78: map['key1'] = 100;  // OK with Record type
79: 
80: // 5. Enums
81: enum Color {
82:   Red,
83:   Green,
84:   Blue
85: }
86: 
87: // 6. Class inheritance
88: class Animal {
89:   name: string = '';
90: }
91: 
92: class Dog extends Animal {
93:   breed: string = '';
94: }
95: 
96: // 7. Generics (basic)
97: class Container<T> {
98:   private value: T = {} as T;
99: 
100:   setValue(value: T): void {
101:     this.value = value;
102:   }
103: 
104:   getValue(): T {
105:     return this.value;
106:   }
107: }
108: ```
109: 
110: ## Type System
111: 
112: ### Primitive Types
113: 
114: ```typescript
115: // Numbers
116: let integer: number = 42;
117: let float: number = 3.14;
118: 
119: // Strings
120: let text: string = 'Hello';
121: let template: string = `Value: ${integer}`;  // Template literals
122: 
123: // Booleans
124: let flag: boolean = true;
125: 
126: // Arrays
127: let numbers: number[] = [1, 2, 3];
128: let strings: Array<string> = ['a', 'b', 'c'];
129: 
130: // Tuples
131: let tuple: [string, number] = ['age', 25];
132: 
133: // Null and undefined (with unions)
134: let nullable: string | null = null;
135: let optional: string | undefined = undefined;
136: 
137: // Resource types (HarmonyOS-specific)
138: let icon: Resource = $r('app.media.icon');
139: let color: Resource = $r('app.color.primary');
140: let string: ResourceStr = $r('app.string.app_name');
141: ```
142: 
143: ### Object Types
144: 
145: ```typescript
146: // Interface (preferred)
147: interface Product {
148:   readonly id: string;  // Read-only
149:   name: string;
150:   price: number;
151:   description?: string;  // Optional
152:   tags?: string[];
153: }
154: 
155: // Implementation
156: const product: Product = {
157:   id: 'prod_001',
158:   name: 'Phone',
159:   price: 999
160: };
161: 
162: // Type alias (for unions, primitives)
163: type Point = {
164:   x: number;
165:   y: number;
166: };
167: 
168: // Nested interfaces
169: interface Address {
170:   street: string;
171:   city: string;
172:   country: string;
173: }
174: 
175: interface UserProfile {
176:   id: string;
177:   name: string;
178:   address: Address;
179: }
180: ```
181: 
182: ### Function Types
183: 
184: ```typescript
185: // Function declarations
186: function add(a: number, b: number): number {
187:   return a + b;
188: }
189: 
190: // Arrow functions
191: const multiply = (a: number, b: number): number => a * b;
192: 
193: // Optional parameters
194: function greet(name: string, greeting?: string): string {
195:   return `${greeting ?? 'Hello'}, ${name}`;
196: }
197: 
198: // Default parameters
199: function createUser(name: string, role: string = 'user'): User {
200:   return { id: '0', name, role };
201: }
202: 
203: // Rest parameters
204: function sum(...numbers: number[]): number {
205:   return numbers.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
206: }
207: 
208: // Callback types
209: type ClickHandler = (event: ClickEvent) => void;
210: 
211: function setOnClick(handler: ClickHandler): void {
212:   // ...
213: }
214: 
215: // Function overloading (limited)
216: function process(input: string): string;
217: function process(input: number): number;
218: function process(input: string | number): string | number {
219:   return input;
220: }
221: ```
222: 
223: ### Generics
224: 
225: ```typescript
226: // Generic function
227: function identity<T>(value: T): T {
228:   return value;
229: }
230: 
231: // With constraints
232: interface HasId {
233:   id: string;
234: }
235: 
236: function findById<T extends HasId>(items: T[], id: string): T | undefined {
237:   return items.find(item => item.id === id);
238: }
239: 
240: // Generic interface
241: interface Repository<T extends HasId> {
242:   getById(id: string): Promise<T>;
243:   save(item: T): Promise<void>;
244:   delete(id: string): Promise<void>;
245: }
246: 
247: // Generic class
248: class Stack<T> {
249:   private items: T[] = [];
250: 
251:   push(item: T): void {
252:     this.items.push(item);
253:   }
254: 
255:   pop(): T | undefined {
256:     return this.items.pop();
257:   }
258: 
259:   peek(): T | undefined {
260:     return this.items[this.items.length - 1];
261:   }
262: 
263:   get length(): number {
264:     return this.items.length;
265:   }
266: }
267: 
268: // Usage
269: const numberStack = new Stack<number>();
270: numberStack.push(1);
271: numberStack.push(2);
272: console.log(numberStack.pop());  // 2
273: ```
274: 
275: ## Classes
276: 
277: ### Class Declaration
278: 
279: ```typescript
280: class User {
281:   // Properties MUST have default values (strict requirement)
282:   private id: string = '';
283:   public name: string = '';
284:   protected email: string = '';
285:   readonly createdAt: Date = new Date();
286: 
287:   // Static members
288:   static userCount: number = 0;
289:   static readonly MAX_USERS: number = 1000;
290: 
291:   // Constructor
292:   constructor(id: string, name: string, email: string) {
293:     this.id = id;
294:     this.name = name;
295:     this.email = email;
296:     User.userCount++;
297:   }
298: 
299:   // Methods
300:   public getDisplayName(): string {
301:     return this.name;
302:   }
303: 
304:   private validateEmail(): boolean {
305:     return this.email.includes('@');
306:   }
307: 
308:   protected getInitials(): string {
309:     return this.name.charAt(0);
310:   }
311: 
312:   // Getter/Setter
313:   get displayName(): string {
314:     return `USER-${this.id}`;
315:   }
316: 
317:   set displayName(value: string) {
318:     // Validate and process
319:     this.name = value;
320:   }
321: 
322:   // Static method
323:   static createGuest(): User {
324:     return new User('guest', 'Guest', 'guest@example.com');
325:   }
326: }
327: ```
328: 
329: ### Property Initializers
330: 
331: ```typescript
332: // ALL properties must have initial values
333: class MyClass {
334:   // ✅ Correct: Has default value
335:   name: string = '';
336:   count: number = 0;
337:   items: string[] = [];
338:   user: User | null = null;
339: 
340:   // ✅ Correct: Initialized in constructor
341:   private value: number;
342: 
343:   constructor(value: number) {
344:     this.value = value;
345:   }
346: 
347:   // ❌ WRONG: No default value
348:   // data: string;  // Compilation Error!
349: }
350: ```
351: 
352: ## Async/Await
353: 
354: ```typescript
355: // Async function
356: async function fetchUser(id: string): Promise<User> {
357:   const response = await httpClient.get<User>(`/users/${id}`);
358:   return response;
359: }
360: 
361: // Error handling
362: async function safeGetUser(id: string): Promise<User | null> {
363:   try {
364:     return await fetchUser(id);
365:   } catch (error) {
366:     console.error(`Failed to fetch user: ${(error as Error).message}`);
367:     return null;
368:   }
369: }
370: 
371: // Parallel execution
372: async function loadDashboard(): Promise<DashboardData> {
373:   const [user, orders, notifications] = await Promise.all([
374:     fetchUser('current'),
375:     fetchOrders(),
376:     fetchNotifications()
377:   ]);
378: 
379:   return { user, orders, notifications };
380: }
381: 
382: // Sequential execution with error handling
383: async function processOrder(orderIds: string[]): Promise<void> {
384:   for (const id of orderIds) {
385:     try {
386:       await processOrder(id);
387:     } catch (error) {
388:       console.error(`Failed to process ${id}:`, error);
389:       // Continue with next order
390:     }
391:   }
392: }
393: ```
394: 
395: ## Best Practices
396: 
397: ### 1. Always Initialize Properties
398: 
399: ```typescript
400: // ❌ BAD
401: class User {
402:   name: string;  // Error: not initialized
403: }
404: 
405: // ✅ GOOD
406: class User {
407:   name: string = '';
408: }
409: 
410: // ✅ ALSO GOOD: Initialize in constructor
411: class User {
412:   name: string;
413: 
414:   constructor(name: string) {
415:     this.name = name;
416:   }
417: }
418: ```
419: 
420: ### 2. Use Explicit Return Types
421: 
422: ```typescript
423: // ❌ BAD
424: function getUser(id: string) {
425:   return { id, name: 'John' };
426: }
427: 
428: // ✅ GOOD
429: function getUser(id: string): User {
430:   return { id, name: 'John' };
431: }
432: ```
433: 
434: ### 3. Prefer Interfaces Over Type Aliases for Objects
435: 
436: ```typescript
437: // ✅ PREFERRED for object types
438: interface User {
439:   id: string;
440:   name: string;
441:   email: string;
442: }
443: 
444: // Use type for unions, primitives, tuples
445: type Status = 'active' | 'inactive';
446: type Coordinate = [number, number];
447: type StringMap = Record<string, string>;
448: ```
449: 
450: ### 4. Use Record for Dynamic Keys
451: 
452: ```typescript
453: // ❌ BAD
454: let cache = {};
455: cache['key'] = value;  // Error!
456: 
457: // ✅ GOOD
458: let cache: Record<string, CacheEntry> = {};
459: cache['key'] = value;  // OK
460: ```
461: 
462: ### 5. Avoid Optional Chaining on Non-Nullable
463: 
464: ```typescript
465: // ❌ BAD: unnecessary optional chaining
466: const user: User = getUser();
467: console.log(user?.name);  // user is not nullable
468: 
469: // ✅ GOOD
470: console.log(user.name);
471: ```
472: 
473: ## Error Handling
474: 
475: ```typescript
476: // Custom error class
477: class AppError extends Error {
478:   constructor(
479:     message: string,
480:     public code: number,
481:     public details?: Object
482:   ) {
483:     super(message);
484:     this.name = 'AppError';
485:   }
486: }
487: 
488: // Throwing errors
489: function validateUser(user: User): void {
490:   if (!user.name) {
491:     throw new AppError('Name is required', 400);
492:   }
493:   if (!user.email.includes('@')) {
494:     throw new AppError('Invalid email', 400, { email: user.email });
495:   }
496: }
497: 
498: // Error handling with try-catch
499: async function loadUserData(): Promise<void> {
500:   try {
501:     const user = await fetchUser('current');
502:     validateUser(user);
503:   } catch (error) {
504:     if (error instanceof AppError) {
505:       console.error(`Error ${error.code}: ${error.message}`);
506:       // Handle specific error
507:     } else if (error instanceof Error) {
508:       console.error(`Unexpected error: ${error.message}`);
509:     } else {
510:       console.error('Unknown error');
511:     }
512:   }
513: }
514: ```
515: 
516: ## Working with null and undefined
517: 
518: ```typescript
519: // Nullish coalescing operator
520: function greet(name: string | null): string {
521:   return name ?? 'Guest';
522: }
523: 
524: // Optional chaining
525: interface User {
526:   address?: {
527:     city?: string;
528:     country?: string;
529:   };
530: }
531: 
532: function getUserCity(user: User | null): string {
533:   return user?.address?.city ?? 'Unknown';
534: }
535: 
536: // Null checks
537: function processValue(value: string | null | undefined): void {
538:   if (value != null) {  // Checks for both null and undefined
539:     console.info(value.length);
540:   }
541: }
542: 
543: // Non-null assertion (use sparingly)
544: function processValue2(value: string | null): void {
545:   // Only use when you're certain value is not null
546:   console.info(value!.length);
547: }
548: ```
